Armani.known: Milanese ease; Acqua di Giò's sea air
Armani.about:
Giorgio Armani founded his house in Milan in 1975 with his partner Sergio Galeotti, and the fragrances have been made with L'Oréal for decades, a partnership now signed through 2050. The scents follow the tailoring: understated, clean-lined and easy to wear every day.
Acqua di Giò pour Homme (1996), composed by Alberto Morillas, is the house's best-known bottle and one of the most worn men's fragrances in the world. Armani/Privé is the couture end of the line, and I Will is the newest signature from the main collection. Giorgio Armani died in September 2025; the house continues under his foundation.

Claude Marsal.about:
Claude Marsal is a young house launched in 2016 and sold through the American retailer J&J Parfums, which lists it among its own signature houses; the brand says its perfumes are made in France. Rather than a famous perfumer's name, the idea behind it is music: blending notes the way a composer builds a harmony, with each scent named for a melody, an instrument or a song.
La Mélodie, Le Piano and the Noir series (Or Noir among them) are the line's pillars, and they lean toward rich, warm compositions at a high concentration. The three we carry are the ones we kept reaching for.

Ferragamo.known: Florentine elegance since the shoemaker to the stars
Ferragamo.about:
Salvatore Ferragamo opened his Florence workshop in 1927 after a decade in Hollywood making shoes for film stars, which earned him the nickname shoemaker to the stars. The house is still family-controlled and still headquartered in Palazzo Spini Feroni on the Arno.
Fragrances arrived in the late 1990s with Ferragamo pour Femme; Signorina (2011) became the commercial pillar. Since 2021 the fragrances have been produced by Inter Parfums through a Florence-based subsidiary, with production in Italy. Uomo Signature is the sharper, leather-and-coffee rework of the house's main men's scent.

Gabriella Antosh.about:
Gabriella Antosh is a small American label that appeared in 2018 with four fragrances at once: Zoltan, Gizella, Gaby and Gaby Blossom, sold through the retailer J&J Parfums. The house publishes no history of its own, and no perfumer is credited on the bottles, so we describe the juice rather than the legend.
Zoltan, the one we carry, is the men's scent of the four: an icy mint-and-grapefruit opening that turns into cinnamon, rose and leather within the hour. It has since become hard to find, which is part of why we keep it in the collection.

Givenchy.known: Parisian couture; the Audrey Hepburn legacy
Givenchy.about:
Hubert de Givenchy founded his couture house in Paris in 1952, and Parfums Givenchy followed in 1957 with L'Interdit, a scent he made for his friend and muse Audrey Hepburn. She wore it privately before it went on sale, became the first actress to front a perfume, and the name comes from her reported protest when told it would be sold: but I forbid you.
Gentleman (1974) is the men's pillar, and Gentleman Réserve Privée is its whisky-and-iris after-dark edition. Givenchy has been part of LVMH since 1988.

Jean Paul Gaultier.about:
Jean Paul Gaultier launched his label in Paris in 1982 and brought the same playfulness to perfume: Classique (1993) in a corseted bust, and Le Male (1995) as a sailor's torso in a striped shirt, sold in a tin can. Le Male, composed by a 26-year-old Francis Kurkdjian, became one of the best-selling men's fragrances ever made.
The Barcelona group Puig has owned the fashion house since 2011 and has produced the fragrances since 2016. Le Male Elixir is the darkest, warmest take on the original, with honeyed vanilla, benzoin and tobacco under the lavender.

Maison Francis Kurkdjian.known: A perfumer's own house; luminous, polished compositions
Maison Francis Kurkdjian.about:
Francis Kurkdjian composed Le Male for Jean Paul Gaultier at 26 and spent the next decade creating for other houses before founding his own in Paris in 2009 with business partner Marc Chaya, in a boutique near Place Vendôme. The house describes its values as purity, sophistication, timelessness and a bold, reinvented classicism.
Baccarat Rouge 540 was commissioned for the crystal maker's 250th anniversary and named for the temperature, 540 °C, at which the crystal is fired; it went on to become a global phenomenon. LVMH took a majority stake in 2017, with Kurkdjian still creative director, and since 2021 he has also directed perfume creation at Dior.

Maison Margiela.about:
Martin Margiela founded his Paris house in 1988, and Replica, launched in 2012, takes its name from his 1994 clothing line that reproduced found vintage garments. Each Replica fragrance recreates a specific memory with a place and a year on the label: Jazz Club is a Brooklyn bar in 2013, Coffee Break a warm café in the cold.
The bottles are plain apothecary flasks with a typewritten cotton label, a nod to the blank white tags on Margiela clothes. The fragrances are made by L'Oréal under licence, and the collection is marketed as genderless, which is exactly how we sell it.

Nishane.about:
Nishane was started in Istanbul in 2012 by Mert Güzel and Murat Katran, and it is the city's first niche perfume house. Almost everything they make is an extrait de parfum, poured at the highest concentration and meant for anyone to wear, which is why so much of this shop's collection comes from them.
Each Nishane collection is a story before it is a smell: the city itself, the Karagöz shadow theatre that gives Hacivat (2017) its name, the poetry of Rumi. Hacivat and Ani (2019) are the two the world knows best, and both have the house's signature of a loud, confident opening settling into something long and warm. Still independent and run by its founders.

Parfums de Marly.about:
Parfums de Marly was founded in Paris in 2009 by Julien Sprecher and takes its name from the Château de Marly, the retreat where Louis XV escaped the etiquette of Versailles. The house emblem honours the Horses of Marly, the sculptures the king commissioned in 1743, and the whole idea is to bring that era's extravagance into perfumes that feel current rather than costumed.
Layton (2016) and Delina (2017) made the house a fixture, with Althaïr (2023) the newest of its icons. Sprecher still leads the creative side; since 2023 the house has been majority-owned by the investment firm Advent International.

Tom Ford.about:
Tom Ford founded his own house in 2005, the year after leaving Gucci, and launched Tom Ford Beauty in 2006 with Black Orchid as its first fragrance. The fragrances have been made by The Estée Lauder Companies from the start, and in 2023 Lauder bought the brand outright.
Private Blend, launched in 2007, is the part of the line that made Tom Ford a name in niche: Tobacco Vanille, Oud Wood and Tuscan Leather all come from that first wave. The house style is rich and unapologetic, with heavy concentrations, dark woods, leather and tobacco in plain black-and-gold bottles.

Valentino.about:
Valentino Garavani founded his house in Rome in 1960 with his partner Giancarlo Giammetti, and Rome has been its creative home ever since. The first Valentino fragrance arrived in 1978; since 2019 the fragrances have been made by L'Oréal under licence.
Born in Roma, launched in 2019, was the first collection under that partnership and is the one this shop carries most of. Inspired by creative director Pierpaolo Piccioli's Rome, the bottles wear the house's Rockstud studs, and each flanker takes the city at a different hour, from Green Stravaganza's sunrise gardens to Purple Melancholia's late nights.

Versace.about:
Gianni Versace opened his first boutique in Milan in 1978, and the house released its first fragrance three years later. After his death in 1997 his siblings Donatella and Santo carried it forward, and the fragrances have been produced by the Milan-area house EuroItalia since 2005.
Eros, launched in 2012 and named for the Greek god of love, became one of the best-selling men's designer fragrances in the world, and Eros Najim is its darker, smokier extension. Bright Crystal (2006) and Dylan Blue (2016) round out the house's most recognised bottles, each with the Medusa on the front.

Xerjoff.known: Perfume as art, rare materials, jewelled flacons
Xerjoff.about:
Xerjoff was formally founded in Turin in 2007 by Sergio Momo and Dominique Salvo, with roots a few years earlier. Momo's idea was perfume as an art object: the rarest natural materials, poured into flacons of hand-polished quartz, semi-precious stone and Murano-style glass with gold caps.
Naxos (2015), Alexandria II (2012) and Erba Pura are the house's best-known scents. Xerjoff also revived Casamorati, a Bolognese perfume house from 1888, and its Shooting Stars collection ships with a certified fragment of meteorite. It remains independent, with Momo as creative director.

Yves Saint Laurent.about:
Yves Saint Laurent and Pierre Bergé founded the couture house in Paris in 1961, and its first fragrance, Y, followed in 1964. Opium (1977) became one of the most famous orientals in perfumery, and the modern men's line, led by La Nuit de L'Homme (2009), carried that sensual, after-dark character into a new era.
The fragrances have been made by L'Oréal since it acquired YSL Beauté in 2008, while the fashion house belongs to Kering. Black Opium (2014) and Libre (2019) are the current pillars on the women's side.
